heroHeadline: Madrid Takes Over Ceuta's Port for Migrant Tents as Police Chief Contradicts Report on Morocco's Role
heroSubtitle: Spain's Transport Ministry authorised the temporary occupation of 16,000 m² at Ceuta's port to house more than 1,000 migrants in tents, overriding a vote by the Port Authority's own board against the installation. The move follows national police chief Francisco Pardo's written denial to Interior Minister Grande-Marlaska that any police report attributes the July 30-31 crossing's planning or execution to Moroccan security forces — directly contradicting the CENIF intelligence document that surfaced Sept 1 — and comes after Sept 2 solidarity protests (roughly 50,000 in Madrid alone) ended in far-right-led rioting outside Congress, with tear gas, rubber bullets, four arrests and RTVE journalists assaulted nationwide. Interior Ministry data separately show Ceuta's land arrivals more than doubled in 2026 even before counting the July surge, and Brussels is dispatching a technical mission to Ceuta after a Marlaska-Brunner call on EU support.
